text: Seven rules chase unfinished work for the whole practice. A manager checks them now and then, and especially in the first week after go-live, to make sure they're running.
The one thing to remember: a red Last run hit a problem line means that rule stopped partway. Tell the admin the same day.
Each rule says what it watches, when it checks, who gets the task, and whether it comes back if it's marked done too early.
Charts, bills, calls and labs are checked at six p.m. Eastern.
This red line says the call rule's last run hit a problem, and when. Some calls may not have become tasks.
An admin can open a rule with Edit.
When it fires: after something has sat a while, or at the end of the day.
Who gets the task, and the queue it waits on when nobody is found.
Whether it comes back if someone marks it done while the work is still open.
And the title and notes staff see on the task.
Changes save as you make them, so close it without touching anything. Done.
Run now checks every rule straight away. Rules that check at six p.m. still wait for six.
The switch turns a rule off. Leave them on unless the owner decides otherwise.
Built-in tasks, like membership renewals and weekly counts, are listed at the bottom. They can't be switched off here.
Practice managers see this page without Edit or Run now, and the switches are locked.

The most common mistakes: switching a rule off to quiet a busy task list, and scrolling past a red problem line. Remember: a red Last run hit a problem line means that rule stopped partway. Tell the admin the same day.
